description:
Nidzica Castle is a Brick Gothic castle of the Teutonic Order in Warmia-Masuria. Wikipedia dates the start of construction to around 1370, while a 2022 study argues that the surviving brick castle was actually built later, in 1399–1409 — the exact date remains genuinely uncertain. What is clear is that the Teutonic pfleger made the castle his residence in 1409, shortly before Polish forces captured it, undefended, on 12 July 1410.

The castle changed hands more than once in the turbulent decades that followed: Polish knights besieged and took it again in 1414, during the Hunger War, and in 1455 Czech troops under Jan Kolda ze Zampachu captured it. Centuries later, a fire in 1784 consumed part of the inner ward, and the French army devastated the castle further in 1812. A rebuilding between 1828 and 1830 repurposed the structure as a court and a prison.

The Soviet army bombarded Nidzica in 1945, leaving it largely in ruins, and reconstruction took place between 1961 and 1965. The castle today houses the Muzeum Ziemi Nidzickiej (Museum of the Nidzica Region) and offers overnight accommodation — a reconstructed castle rather than an untouched medieval survivor.

A fire consumed the inner ward in 1784 and the French army devastated the castle in 1812; in 1828–1830 it was rebuilt as a court and prison. The Soviet army bombarded it in 1945, and reconstruction took place between 1961 and 1965.

faqs.question: Is Nidzica the same as Niedzica Castle?
faqs.answer: No. Nidzica Castle is a Teutonic castle in Warmia-Masuria; Niedzica Castle is a different castle on Lake Czorsztyn in Lesser Poland, covered at [Niedzica Castle](/castles/poland/niedzica-castle).

faqs.question: How old is Nidzica Castle?
faqs.answer: Wikipedia dates the start of construction to around 1370, while a 2022 study argues for 1399–1409; sources differ.

meta_description: Stay at Nidzica Castle in Warmia-Masuria, Poland — a Brick Gothic Teutonic castle, rebuilt 1961–1965, with a museum. From approx. €66/night.

hotel.non_guest_access_note: The castle is also open to day visitors as a museum — check current opening times with the castle.
hotel.room_location_note: Rooms are in Zamek Nidzica, the castle hotel at ul. Zamkowa 2
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** At ul. Zamkowa 2 in Nidzica, in the Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €66/night for a Double Room with two twin beds, a private bathroom and an inner-courtyard view, taxes included, with free cancellation on the rate seen. Breakfast is about €8 extra. A Standard Queen Room starts around €73 and a Superior Apartment around €87.

**On-site:** The castle also houses a museum, and the forecourt and courtyard can be seen on a day visit.

**Good to know:** The castle was bombarded in 1945 and left largely in ruins until it was reconstructed between 1961 and 1965, so expect a rebuilt castle. Breakfast is charged separately, and the cheapest rooms look onto the inner courtyard.

**Combine with:** [Olsztyn Castle](/castles/poland/olsztyn-castle-warmia) and [Ryn Castle](/castles/poland/ryn-castle), elsewhere in Warmia and Masuria.
